learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the special helper verbs that change the mood of a sentence to show ability, permission, or possibility!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Auxiliary verbs are the ultimate helpers! They cannot stand alone, so they team up with main verbs to show tense and form questions. The main helpers are 'be', 'do', and 'have'.
Modals are a special type of helper verb. They change the whole mood of the sentence! Words like 'can', 'could', 'may', 'might', 'must', and 'should' are magical modals.
Use 'can' to talk about ability: 'I CAN jump high.' Use 'may' to politely ask for permission: 'MAY I go to the washroom?' Using the right one makes you sound super smart!
Use 'must' when there is a strict rule or obligation, like 'You MUST wear a seatbelt.' Use 'should' to give friendly advice, like 'You SHOULD eat more vegetables.'

fun_activity.title: 👑 The King's Rules Game
fun_activity.instructions: Pretend you are the King or Queen of a new country! Write down three rules using 'Must' (strict laws) and two pieces of advice using 'Should' for your citizens.

quick_recap: ⭐ Auxiliary verbs help the main verb show time or form a question.
⭐ Modal verbs are special helpers that express ability, permission, possibility, and strong advice.
